observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show the same solar panel from slightly different angles.
The panel has a white frame and black photovoltaic cells arranged in a grid of 6 columns and 10 rows (60 cells total).
The cells are rounded at the corners, typical of monocrystalline or polycrystalline panels.
There is a watermark 'MIMI SOLAR POSTED ON JIJI' overlaid on both photos.
No brand or model label is visible on the front or edges of the panel in either photo.
The panel is leaning against a wall in an outdoor or semi-outdoor setting with wet ground, suggesting possible exposure to moisture or rain.

claims.claim: Mimi solar enterprise do in all kind of solar energy, solar panels, inverters, solar chest freezer, ...
claims.evidence: The seller's text claims they sell various solar products, but the photos show only one solar panel. No inverters, freezers, or other products are visible. The watermark 'MIMI SOLAR' may indicate the seller's brand, but it is not proof of the full range of products.

risks.risk: The solar panel may be damaged or defective, such as cracked cells, delamination, or internal wiring issues.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the panel's surface showing the cells in detail, especially under bright light, to check for cracks or discoloration. Also, a photo of the backside and junction box to check for damage or moisture ingress.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially non-functional or low-efficiency

risks.risk: The panel's power output (wattage) is unknown, which is critical for pricing.
risks.proof: A photo of the label on the back of the panel showing the model, wattage, voltage, and manufacturer details.
risks.if_unproven: priced as low-wattage or unknown-efficiency panel

risks.risk: The panel may be counterfeit or of poor quality, especially if the brand is not identifiable.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the back label or any certification marks (e.g., IEC, CE, TUV) to verify authenticity and quality standards.

proof_requests: Photo of the back of the solar panel showing the label with model, wattage, and manufacturer details.
Close-up photo of the front cells under bright light to check for cracks or defects.
Photo of the junction box and backside to check for damage or moisture.
Photo of any certification marks or quality labels.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a solar panel, but critical details such as wattage, brand, and condition are missing. Without proof of these, the panel cannot be accurately priced, and risks of damage or low quality cannot be ruled out.
